where_the_unledgered_answers_come_from.finding: NO WORKFLOW IN THIS REPOSITORY COMMITS UNDER THAT IDENTITY. All ten workflows that commit declare a bot name — chatgpt-usage-monitor[bot], claude-usage-monitor[bot], gumroad-monitor[bot], itch-monitor[bot], listing-sync[bot], pulse[bot] — and laps commit as Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>. where_the_unledgered_answers_come_from.the_signature_that_separates_them: Every bot and lap commit is stamped +00:00. All six unledgered answers are stamped +09:00 (JST), author equal to committer, one file changed, and an English sentence-case message ('Add Codex verification result for 2026-08-10.w'). That is a consistent second producer, not an occasional hand relay: a person pasting six files over seven hours would not hold that shape while every other commit in the repository holds the other one.
where_the_unledgered_answers_come_from.what_this_changes: Two things that were resting on the ledger. (1) 'Re-run the task under a fresh task_id so the workflow writes a ledger entry' — the standing repair in the .n entry — CANNOT establish who wrote the original: it would establish who wrote the RE-RUN. The two producers are different, so the answers are not comparable by re-running. (2) Which weekly ChatGPT window a given answer spent is confounded, because state/usage.json meters an account and the ledger only sees one of the two paths that spend it. scripts/spark-model.mjs settles 'did naming Spark work' by reading which window moved; that reading is only sound for answers the ledger actually saw.
where_the_unledgered_answers_come_from.what_is_still_unknown: Which product the second path is (ChatGPT agent mode, Codex cloud, or the owner acting through either), and whether it reads codex/INBOX.md on a schedule or on demand. Nothing readable from inside this repository distinguishes those, and none of them changes the two consequences above.
